content:
D&O insurance protects administrators, directors and board members when someone claims compensation from them personally for a management decision. Within the limits and conditions of the policy, the insurer can pay for the legal defence and the amount owed. In Moldova this policy is, as a rule, voluntary.

What D&O insurance covers

D&O stands for "Directors and Officers", meaning directors and people in management positions. The policy comes into play when a company, a member or shareholder, a creditor or an authority raises a claim about how a person ran the business. Typical examples are a disputed payment, a loss-making contract or incorrect financial reporting.

As a rule, the policy can include:

  • Lawyers' fees and court costs.
  • The amount set by a judgment or by a settlement accepted by the insurer.
  • Defence costs in an investigation by an authority, if the policy provides for it.
  • Former directors, for decisions made during their mandate, if they are included.

The list of insured persons and covered situations is read in the offer. Law No. 92/2022 on insurance and reinsurance activity has no separate class for D&O. The closest reference is class 13, "General liability insurance", while legal defence may fall under class 17. The insurer confirms the exact classification.

When an administrator is personally liable

A company has its own assets, but the law can also direct a claim at the person who ran it. Three laws matter for company management:

LawWho it concernsWhat it provides, in short
Law No. 135/2007, Article 76The administrator of an LLCFull material liability for damage caused to the company, including through unlawful payments to members. Several administrators are jointly and severally liable, unless the court decides otherwise.
Law No. 1134/1997, Article 73Officers of a joint-stock companyThey answer for damage caused to the company and, among other things, for deliberately hiding or distorting financial information.
Law No. 149/2012, Article 248Members of the management bodies of an insolvent debtor and others who caused the insolvencyOn request, the court may order them to bear part of the debts, if they caused the insolvency through the acts listed in the law.

A claim does not prove fault. Even an unfounded claim, however, can mean months of defence and costs the person carries alone if the company does not take them on. This is where the policy has practical value.

Who needs D&O

Company situationWhere a claim may come from
Several members or shareholdersA member or shareholder challenges a management decision
Investors, or a subsidiary within a groupThe investor or the group asks for an account of results or reporting
A hired director with no ownership stakeThe company or new owners claim compensation
Large loans or financial difficultiesCreditors or the insolvency administrator
Activity in a regulated sectorAn authority opens a review of management

The risk is not only a matter of company size. Hypothetical example: in an LLC with two members, the administrator approves a large payment to a supplier, and the work is never carried out. After a change of members, the new management asks the administrator to cover the loss. The administrator needs a lawyer and the documents behind the decision, even if the case is eventually won. A D&O policy can, under its conditions, take on the defence costs and the amount set, provided it does not exclude claims brought by the company or its members.

A policy does not replace good organisation. Resolutions of members or shareholders, minutes and records of important decisions help the defence and show the insurer how the company is run.

Some lenders, investors or foreign partners may require the policy by contract. Before a financing agreement is signed, the documents are checked for such a requirement.

How D&O differs from other insurance

An ordinary general liability policy usually concerns bodily injury and property damage caused to others by the company's activity. Professional liability concerns errors in services provided to clients. D&O concerns management decisions and the people who make them. A company may need several policies, with a written boundary between them. IT incidents are reviewed under cyber insurance.

What is not usually paid

  • Damage caused intentionally, fraud and unlawful personal gain, usually after a final judgment.
  • Fines and criminal penalties.
  • Facts and claims the applicant knew or should have known about when the policy was taken out.
  • Claims related to insolvency, if the policy excludes or limits them.
  • Bodily injury and property damage, which belong to other insurance.
  • Personal debts unrelated to the position.
  • Some claims between insured persons or from the company itself, if the policy excludes them.

Article 1874 of the Civil Code provides that the insured has no right to compensation to the extent that the insured acted with the intention of causing that damage. Some of the acts in Article 248 of the Insolvency Law may meet this condition, in which case the policy may not pay the final amount. Whether it can pay for the defence until judgment is checked separately.

Why the date of the claim matters

D&O policies are usually tied to the moment a claim is made and reported to the insurer, not to the date of the disputed decision. A decision from 2024 can be challenged in 2026. In that case the policy in force in 2026 is examined, if 2024 falls within the accepted period, and, if the claim falls within the additional period, so is the policy that expired earlier. For this reason three things are checked:

  • From what date earlier decisions are accepted.
  • Whether this date is kept when the insurer changes.
  • What happens after the policy expires or a director leaves, and how a situation that may lead to a claim is reported.

For policies tied to the making of a claim, Article 1878(2) of the Civil Code includes claims made within an additional period at least equal to the limitation period applicable to the liability, if they are based on a fact that occurred before the insurance period ended. A shorter period in the policy is analysed against this rule before signing.

Sum insured, premium and documents for an offer

The sum insured is chosen according to the size of the company, its debts, the number of members or shareholders and the real risks. It is checked whether the amount is shared by all persons and claims in the policy period, and whether lawyers' fees and court costs reduce it or are paid on top of it. The premium depends on the line of business, financial position, ownership structure, litigation history and the amount chosen.

  • The insurer's questionnaire, completed and signed.
  • The ownership structure and the group structure.
  • The list of management positions to be insured.
  • Financial statements for recent years.
  • Known disputes, investigations, claims and financial difficulties.
  • The insurance requirement from contracts, if there is one.

Sensitive legal documents are sent through the channel agreed with the broker. According to the National Bank of Moldova's report for 2025, motor insurance accounts for more than 71.6% of general insurance premiums, and the report has no separate data for D&O. The availability of the product and its conditions are confirmed for each company. The National Bank of Moldova supervises the market (Article 4 of Law No. 92/2022).

What an administrator does on receiving a claim

  1. Keeps the letter, summons or notice and the date of receipt.
  2. Notifies the insurer without delay (Article 1851 of the Civil Code) and meets the deadline in the policy.
  3. Gathers the documents on the disputed decision and meets the deadlines in the summons or notice.
  4. Agrees the lawyer and defence costs with the insurer, if the policy requires this.
  5. Discusses any admission or settlement with the insurer first. A clause releasing the insurer merely because of an admission is void (Article 1875(1) of the Civil Code), but an agreement the insurer has not consented to does not bind the insurer (paragraph 2).

The role of the broker and the insurer

The broker reviews the company's structure, prepares the file, requests offers from licensed insurers, depending on the risk, and compares the conditions on the same basis. When a claim arises, the broker assists with the notification and communication with the insurer. The insurer accepts the risk, sets the premium and conditions and decides on payment.

Frequently asked questions about D&O insurance

Is D&O insurance mandatory in Moldova?

As a rule, no. The company decides whether to take out a policy for the people who run it. A requirement may come from a financing agreement, from investors or from the group the company belongs to. For a regulated activity, the special law applicable to that activity is also checked.

Can the administrator of an LLC be personally liable?

Yes, under the conditions of the law. Article 76 of Law No. 135/2007 provides for the administrator's full material liability for damage caused to the company. In insolvency, Article 248 of Law No. 149/2012 allows the court, on request, to place part of the debts on management members who caused the insolvency through the acts listed in the law.

How does D&O differ from general liability?

An ordinary general liability policy usually concerns bodily injury and property damage caused to others by the company's activity. D&O concerns claims linked to management decisions and the people who made them, including financial losses. A company may need both policies, with separate limits and conditions for each one.

Does the policy cover a decision made before signing?

It may, under the conditions of the policy. The contract can exclude circumstances the applicant knew or should have known about when it was concluded. If the policy has a date from which earlier decisions are accepted, this limit is also checked, especially when the insurer changes.

Are former directors protected?

They can be protected for decisions made during their mandate, if the policy includes them and the claim is made in the insurance period or the additional period. Before a director leaves, the company is sold or its activity ends, it is checked what happens to the cover and how long claims can still be reported.

What happens when a claim is received?

The person keeps the document and the date of receipt, notifies the insurer without delay and gathers the papers on the disputed decision. The lawyer, costs and any admission or settlement are first discussed with the insurer. Under Article 1875(2) of the Civil Code, a third-party agreement made without the insurer's consent does not bind it.
